author: reek
body: The flash bank lifecycle, done right. A bank is unlocked once, two pages are programmed into it, and it is sealed once, threading the linear handle through every step.

author: reek
body: The seal returns 0, and that is the assertion: a bank reports its own soundness at seal time. Every page write polled the controller's busy flag and found it ready, so no write was lost and the fault count is zero. A negative answer would be the count of pages whose busy-wait ran out of fuel.

author: reek
body: The register writes are real memory-mapped stores (the base is inside mapped RAM), so this exercises the honest MMIO path, not a stub.

author: reek
body: The four adversarial counterparts are errors/hal-flash-leak, errors/hal-flash-double-seal, errors/hal-flash-use-after-seal, and errors/flash-launder-mmio -- the last being the capability gate itself: Device.Mmio is the mechanism and cannot buy the authority.
